4. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the suit land appertaining to an area of 0.05 acres in plot No. 931 under CS khatian No. 242 corresponding to SA Khatian No. 229 and 0.06 acres in both former and present plot No. 931/969 of mouza Dasadi under both District and police station Chandpur has been owning and possessing by Durga Kumar Chakraborty and others from their predecessor namely, Shamkanti Das alias Shamcharan Chakraborty that the plaintiff, namely Gazi Nur Mohammad (now dead) brought Title Suit No. 324 of 1958 in the court of Munsif, first court at Chandqur ( relating to non, suit land) for specific performance of contract, whereupon the decree was passed on 4-4-1961 in favour of the plaintiff with Taka 417.50 as cost; that thereafter said Nur Mohammad obtained registered deed on 11-5-1963 through court: that Nur Mohammad, then filed an execution Case bearing No. 72 of 1963 for realisation of the alleged cost money; that the plaintiff also purchased the land in suit along with other land in auction as highest bidder and also took Bainama on 26-1-1992; that 931 Khatian was mentioned wrongly in that execution case in place of correct CS khatian No. 242 or SA khatian No. 229 and plot No.931-931/969 but the boundary mentioned in auction was intact and that the possession of the land was handed over to plaintiff on 30-4-1992 with performing all formalities of auction sale and thus the case for execution of decree bearing No. 72 of 1963 was disposed of on 31-5-1992 with full satisfaction and since then the plaintiff has been possessing and enjoying its interest by himself as well as by his tenants. It is further stated that the plaintiff namely, GaziNur Mohammad died during pendency of Execution case No. 72 of 1963 and his heirs namely, Hayet-un-nessa and others were substituted in the case; that the defendant refused and threw challenge over the right and status of the plaintiff on the suit land on 16-9-1994 on the basis of a decree in a title suit bearing No. 468 of 1982 and also threatened to dispossess them and for which the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 128 of 1994 for permanent injunction; that the suit was filed in wrong forum for which he finally withdrew the same. It is further stated that the Deputy Commissioner and others on behalf of the government of Bangladesh filed another suit being No. 34 of 1992 praying for declaring the alleged auction and the decree in execution case No. 72 of 1963 as illegal, not binding upon and collusive but the suit was ultimately dismissed. 

 5. The defendant No. 1 namely Abdus Satter Mizi who is present petitioner and on behalf of Government, defendant Nos. 5 and 6 i.e. Deputy Commissioner and Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) Chandpur respectively contested the suit by filing written statement separately. The case of the defendant No.1, in short, is that the total area of land in khatian No. 242 is 12 decimals containing 5 decimals in plot No. 931 and 7 decimals in plot No.931/969 has been owning and possessing by Shamkanto Das and Nibaran Chandra Das, eight annas each, as Rayeti interest and later on Shamkanto Das sold his portion to one Suresh Chandra Chakraborty and accordingly, SA khatian was published in their names; that the defendant took lease on 2 decimals of land including shops thereon in plot No. 931 and that Suresh Chandra Chakraborty left this country and went to India, as such, this defendant took lease of the property, left by Suresh Chandra Chakraborty from Sub-Divisional Officer, vide VP Case No. 8/82-83 and paying rent thereof from 1373 BS to 1380 BS at the rate of Taka 400 per year and from 1381 BS to 1389 BS at the rate of Taka 800 per year. This defendant also paid UP tax and doing business procuring licence and setting electric meter thereto. 

 8. The defendant Nos. 5 and 6, on behalf of the Government, stated in their written statement that the suit land measuringan area of 0.05 acres in plot No. 931 under SA khatian No. 229 and Mouza 18 Dasadi under police station and District Chandpur and 0.06 acres in plot No. 931/969 is vested property; that 0,02 acres of land of plot No. 931 and 0.03 acres of plot No. 931/969 i.e. in total 0.05 acres of land has been leased out to defendant No: 1 vide LA Case No. 08 of 1982-83; that LA Case No.3 of 1981-83; that 21 of 1982-83 and that since the lease property is under possession and control of government, the case of the plaintiff should be dismissed. 

 11. The plaintiff filed a certified copy of CS khatian marked Exhibit 1, a copy Of SA khatian marked Exhibit 2, certified copy of judgment of the suit No. 324 of 1958 marked as Exhibit 3, Original registered deed No. 4239 dated 11-5-1963 with respect to title execution case No.7 of 1962 marked as Exhibit 4, Petition for the title execution case No. 72 of 1963 in the Munsif, First Court, Chandpur marked Exhibit-5, Original Boinama as regard auction purchase in said execution case marked Exhibit 6, certified copy of writ of execution marked Exhibit 6(ka), certified copy of the plaint of title suit No. 34 of 1992 marked Exhibit 7(ka), certified copy of the order dated 7-7-1992 of suit marked as Exhibit 7 (kha), information slip as regard title suit No. 468 of 1982 marked Exhibit 8 and certified copy of the judgment of the Additional District Judge in Miscellaneous Appeal No.9 in 1995 marked Exhibit 9 in support of his contention. 

 12. On the other hand, defendant No. 1 has submitted certified copy of CS khatian No. 242 marked Exhibit-Ka, certified copy of the SA khatian No. 229 marked as Exhibit ka(1), report dated 21-8-1982 by Tahashilder in VP Case marked as Exhibit- Kha, 2 sheets of DCR as regard rent marked Exhibit-GA, One trade licence marked Exhibit-Gha, certified copy of the judgment and decree in title suit No. 71 of 1985 marked as Exhibit-Oma, certified copy of the order of Civil Revision No. 247 of 1886 (Comilla)/8916 of 1991 (Dhaka) dated 27-3-1994 marked Exhibit-Cha and certified copy of the order dated 19-5-1994 in his case marked Exhibit- Cha(1) in support of his contention. 

 18. Mr Abul Hossain Sarder, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the learned trial Court after considering the facts and material on record having found that the Schedule of the auction purchased land as per boinama as Exhibit 6 dated 26-1-1992 does not tally or is not identical with the suit land as mentioned in the, schedule of the plaint and thus dismissed the suit; that the learned appellate Court without considering the schedule of the boinama held that the suit land is identical with the schedule of the boinama that the trial Court having found that the identity of the suit land having riot been established by local investigation, the suit cannot be decreed and accordingly, dismissed the suit and that, on the other hand, the appellate Court though found that the khatian No. 931 in the boinama was wrong but held that the boundary of the auction purchased land was properly given-in the, boinama overlooking the fact that only the north and south boundary have been mentioned, not all sides have been mentioned in the said boinama and thus the learned appellate Court committed an error in allowing the appeal. He 'further submits that the learned trial Court considering the evidence of PWs and DWs held that the plaintiff failed to prove his possession in the suit land and thus dismissed the suit; that the learned. Appellate Court did not consider properly the evidence of PWS and DWs on record and committed an error of law in allowing the appeal holding that since the plaintiff go possession the suit land before, through court in execution case, there is little scope for ascertaining possession further and that the learned appellate Court committed an error in allowing appeal occasioning failure of justice; 

 24. Now we come back to our revision in which pertinent question that calls for our determination is, whether the petitioner actually auction purchased the suit land on 22-10-1991 although there was some wrong in plot arid khatian. 

 30. The moot point for determination is, whether the plaintiff actually got possession of the suit land through auction purchase is admitted that there were some mistakes both in execution case and boinama. But in the boinama there was mentioning of boundary in two sides. The consistent view of our Apex court is that the case of dispute between the plot and khatian, boundary will prevail. Our Appellate Division in the case of Mofizullah Bhuiyan and others vs Sree Narayan Chandra Roy and others reported in 3 MLR (AD) 196 held that when the plaintiffs succeed in proving their title and possession in the suit, land, they are entitled to get a decree for declaration of his title therein. The suit cannot be dismissed merely on the ground of minor variations in the description of the boundaries of the suit land. 

 31. In the instant case, though there is some variations in plot and khatian but there is boundary in the boinama which proves that the suit land is identical with the auction purchased land. Moreover, the present petitioner who is a lessee has no legal right raised this point of variation as the government lost in suit No. 34 of 1992 on this point and the government did not appeal to the higher court against the judgment and decree and thus the government or his lessee is debarred from raising this point any more.
